title: FastAPI Project Structure: Routers, Services and Settings
summary: Quick revision notes on splitting a FastAPI app with APIRouter and include_router, laying out routers, schemas, models and services, centralizing config in a settings module, and avoiding circular imports.

chapters.title: APIRouter Mental Model
points: APIRouter is a mini FastAPI app: it holds path operations (@router.get/post) but cannot run on its own; it must be attached to an app with include_router
One router per resource or domain (users, items, orders), each in its own module, so main.py only wires things together
Router constructor options: APIRouter(prefix='/users', tags=['users'], dependencies=[Depends(get_current_user)], responses={404: {'description': 'Not found'}})
Prefix must start with '/' and must not end with '/'; paths inside the router are relative to the prefix, e.g. @router.get('/{user_id}') becomes /users/{user_id}
Minimal example: router = APIRouter(prefix='/items', tags=['items']); @router.get('/') async def list_items(): ...

chapters.title: Prefix, Tags, Dependencies and include_router
points: app.include_router(router) registers all the router's routes on the app; call it once per router, in main.py or an api/__init__ aggregator
include_router accepts prefix, tags, dependencies and responses that are ADDED on top of those set on the APIRouter, so one router can be mounted under /v1 and /v2 without editing it
Tags group endpoints in the OpenAPI docs only; they do not change routing or behaviour, and tags combine (router tags plus include_router tags plus per-route tags)

Router-level dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)] run for every route in the router, before the path operation's own dependencies; their return values are discarded, so use them for auth checks and side effects only
Nesting works: parent.include_router(child, prefix='/admin') then app.include_router(parent, prefix='/api/v1'), giving /api/v1/admin/...; the final path is the concatenation of all prefixes
Gotcha: include_router copies the routes at call time, so routes added to a router AFTER it was included are missing; define all routes before including

chapters.title: Organizing a Larger App
points: Typical layout: app/main.py, app/api/routers/ (users.py, items.py), app/schemas/ (Pydantic models), app/models/ (SQLAlchemy ORM), app/services/ (business logic), app/core/ (config.py, security.py), app/db/ (session.py, base.py), tests/
Router layer: parse the request, declare Depends, call a service, return a response_model; keep no business logic or raw SQL in route functions
Service layer: plain functions or classes taking a db session and schemas, returning models; testable without HTTP and reusable from CLI or background jobs

schemas vs models: schemas (Pydantic) define the API contract (UserCreate, UserRead with from_attributes=True); models (ORM) define DB tables; never return ORM objects without a response_model, and never expose password hashes

Flow of data: request body → schema in router → service → ORM model → DB, then model → response_model schema → JSON. Group by layer for small apps, or by feature (users/router.py, users/schemas.py, users/service.py) for large ones

chapters.title: Settings Module with pydantic-settings
points: Install pydantic-settings (separate package in Pydantic v2); class Settings(BaseSettings) with typed fields such as database_url: str, debug: bool = False, secret_key: str
Load from env and .env: model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env'); environment variables override .env values, which override field defaults; names are case-insensitive
Create one instance in app/core/config.py (settings = Settings()) and import it everywhere, or wrap in @lru_cache def get_settings() to avoid re-reading .env on every call
Inject with Depends(get_settings) so tests can override via app.dependency_overrides[get_settings] = lambda: Settings(database_url='sqlite://')
Missing required field raises ValidationError at startup, which is the desired fail-fast behaviour; never commit .env, give secrets no default, and use SecretStr to hide values in logs

chapters.title: Avoiding Circular Imports and Common Mistakes
points: Circular import cause: users.py imports items.py which imports users.py, so one module sees a partially initialized module and raises ImportError or AttributeError
Enforce one-way dependency direction: routers → services → models/schemas → core/db; lower layers never import from higher layers, and routers never import each other
Shared pieces (get_db, get_current_user, settings) live in a neutral module such as app/api/deps.py or app/core, imported by routers, never defined in a router

Break unavoidable cycles with imports inside the function, `from __future__ import annotations` plus `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports for type hints only, or by string references in ORM relationship('Item')

Mistakes: instantiating the app in a module other modules import from (import app from main), forgetting prefix leading slash, route '/' with trailing-slash redirect surprises, putting business logic in routers, calling Settings() in many places

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Structuring a FastAPI App
points: Router: router = APIRouter(prefix='/users', tags=['users'], dependencies=[Depends(auth)])
Mount: app.include_router(users.router, prefix='/api/v1'); extra prefix, tags and dependencies stack on top
Layers: router (HTTP) → service (logic) → model (DB) with schema (contract) at the boundaries
Settings: class Settings(BaseSettings) → settings = Settings() or @lru_cache get_settings; env overrides .env overrides defaults
Imports flow one way (routers → services → models → core); shared deps in deps.py; TYPE_CHECKING for type-only cycles
